A_marketable_ioc_fill.setup: Static book (bid 10.00/100, ask 10.02/100); constant_order_latency(70ms,70ms); power_prob_queue_model(2.0); no_partial_fill_exchange. IOC buy limit submitted at ask+$0.01 collar.
A_marketable_ioc_fill.hand_expectation: FILLED at 10.02 (ack_new's price_tick>=best_ask_tick branch fires purely from L1 best-ask depth)

B_ioc_expiry.setup: Same book; order priced off ask=10.02 (limit 10.03) submitted at 50ms; ask re-quotes to 10.06 at 100ms, before the order's 70ms entry latency lands it at the exchange at 120ms.
B_ioc_expiry.hand_expectation: EXPIRED (10.03 < prevailing ask 10.06 at arrival; IOC/FOK do not rest, per nopartialfillexchange.rs ack_new else-branch)

C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.setup: Resting GTC buy at bid=10.00 (qty 20 ahead); five TRADE_EVENT prints of qty 10 at 10.00, once with SELL_EVENT (aggressor hits the bid) and once with no side bit at all (our L1/SIP reality).
C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.hand_expectation: with_side: FILLED (queue_model.trade() consumes queue ahead via EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT, matching the resting Side::Buy order). without_side: stays NEW (a bare TRADE_EVENT matches neither EXCH_BUY_TRADE_EVENT nor EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT in nopartialfillexchange.rs, so it is silently dropped and queue_model.trade() is never called).
C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.actual_result: with_side: FILLED, exec_qty=5.0. without_side: NEW, exec_qty=0.0 -- matches

source_citations: docs/data.rst (qty==0 at a DEPTH_EVENT price removes that level)

feasible_for: Order acceptance/rejection logic driven by top-of-book crossing (marketable IOC/limit fills, GTX/limit rejection at the touch)
IOC/FOK immediate-fill-or-expire semantics, decided purely from best-bid/best-ask depth
Constant and per-symbol latency modelling (entry + response), independent of depth granularity
FlatPerTradeFeeModel / TradingValueFeeModel cost accounting on realized fills
not_feasible_or_meaningless_for: Probabilistic queue-position models (RiskAdverse/Power/Log) that key off trade-print volume at the touch: hftbacktest's exchange models only apply a trade to queue depletion when the event carries a BUY_EVENT/SELL_EVENT aggressor bit (EXCH_BUY_TRADE_EVENT/EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT). Alpaca's consolidated SIP tape has no aggressor side, so these models silently receive zero trade-driven queue depletion under L1 data -- demonstrated empirically in Scenario C, not just asserted.
The L3 FIFO queue model, which needs individual order add/cancel/execute events (order_id-level), categorically unavailable from L1 or even standard L2 SIP quotes.
Any depth-percentile / multi-level queue heuristic that reads levels beyond the touch (our L1 feed only ever has one level per side).
l1_feasibility_verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading hftbacktest/src/backtest/proc/nopartialfillexchange.rs (the exchange model used) and reproducing both code paths (depth-crossing fill/expiry vs trade-driven queue depletion) with a hand-verified synthetic fixture; the L1-driven paths matched hand computation exactly, and the side-dependent path was empirically shown to be a no-op without an aggressor bit.
